lines.text: I looked up at the smoke detector over my bunk.
A tiny red *light.*
We were being watched. Every day. Maybe from the very first one.
So for the cameras, we acted alone.
I ate alone. I exercised alone. I talked to no one.
We only talked at night, in the dark, in Morse.
On a recording, it just sounded like the metal creaking.
Channel 9 called again.
This is Ground. Open Hatch 3.
Now I understood. It was a test. Would we obey a voice that sounded like it was in charge?
We gave it nothing.
Not a word. Not a knock.
Day two hundred ten. Envelope seven.
Locker 7. Two spare scrubber cartridges. You'll know who needs them.
Two cartridges. On my side.
Hale knew there would be two of us. He knew all along.
Around day two hundred twenty, Mara's knocks got slower.
She made mistakes. Letters in the wrong order.
A scrubber pulls carbon dioxide out of the air. When it fails, the CO2 builds up.
First headaches. Then confusion. Then sleep.
And she was on the other side of a door I had promised never to open.
Day two hundred forty. Envelope eight.
By now you know you're not alone. I'm sorry. I couldn't stop it.
That night, three letters. Very slow.
C.
O.
Her scrubber had *failed.*
